title: Decoupling Josephson Coupling and Supercurrent Nonreciprocity in Twisted NbSe2/NbSe2 van der Waals Junctions
authors: Seung-Gi Lee, Kwon-Neong Jung, Jae-Kuen Kim, Jae-Chun Jeon, Jiho Yoon, Stuart S. P. Parkin, Kun-Rok Jeon
abstract: The microscopic origin of supercurrent nonreciprocity in van der Waals Josephson junctions remains under active debate, particularly regarding the role of twist-angle engineering in layered superconductors. Here, we investigate superconducting transport in twisted NbSe2/NbSe2 vertical Josephson junctions fabricated by dry transfer with controlled crystallographic alignment and chemically clean interfaces. High-resolution transmission electron microscopy is employed to directly determine the twist angle and assess interface quality. While the Josephson coupling strength exhibits a pronounced dependence on twist angle, with characteristic voltages maximized near crystallographically equivalent orientations and suppressed at intermediate angles, the supercurrent diode efficiency remains negligibly small and shows no systematic twist-angle dependence. In contrast, enhanced diode-like responses emerge only in weakly coupled junctions exhibiting interfacial disorder and reduced transparency. Deliberate interface degradation further amplifies the apparent nonreciprocity, yielding diode efficiencies approaching 30% together with an irregular magnetic-field-strength dependence. These results establish a clear decoupling between Josephson coupling and supercurrent nonreciprocity in twisted NbSe2/NbSe2 junctions. Our findings identify interface disorder, rather than twist-angle-controlled momentum matching, as the dominant origin of the observed diode response and provide a critical benchmark for interpreting nonreciprocal superconducting transport in van der Waals Josephson devices.
summary: The authors investigated twisted $	ext{NbSe}_2/	ext{NbSe}_2$ junctions to determine if crystal alignment controls supercurrent diode effects. They found that while the primary Josephson coupling strength strongly depends on the twist angle due to momentum matching, the non-reciprocity remains negligible unless interface disorder is intentionally introduced. This decisively decouples the two phenomena, identifying interfacial quality as the source of apparent diode behavior.
main_problem: The study aims to decouple Josephson coupling strength from supercurrent nonreciprocity (diode effect) in twisted van der Waals superconducting junctions, resolving debates on the role of twist angle engineering.
main_result: Josephson coupling shows a clear dependence on twist angle due to momentum matching, but the diode response is found to be negligible unless significant interface disorder is introduced. This establishes that interface disorder, not crystal alignment, dominates non-reciprocity.
method: The research uses electrical transport measurements (I-V curves) combined with structural characterization (HR-TEM) on fabricated twisted NbSe2/NbSe2 junctions.
model_or_system: The physical system is a vertical Josephson junction formed by stacking two layers of Niobium Diselenide ($	ext{NbSe}_2$) with controlled twist angles. Analysis involves comparing measurements to the Ambegaokar-Baratoff relation and using the RCSJ model for dynamics.
key_observables: Josephson coupling strength ($I_c$), supercurrent diode efficiency ($\eta$), critical current ($I_{c\pm}$), and characteristic voltage $V_c$ as functions of twist angle, magnetic field, and temperature.
important_parameters: Twist angle ($	heta_{	ext{twist}}$), in-plane magnetic field ($\mu_0H_{\parallel}$), junction capacitance ($C_{	ext{eff}}$), and interface disorder level.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the RCSJ model for dynamic characterization, and it assumes that deviations from ideal behavior can be attributed to specific physical mechanisms like interface degradation or momentum mismatch.
figures_summary: Figures detail $V-I$ and $dV/dI$ contour maps showing field and angle dependence; Figure 5 specifically plots the distinct $	heta_{	ext{twist}}$ dependence of coupling strength versus nonreciprocity ($\eta$).
paper_structure: The paper systematically investigates transport properties by first establishing the twist-angle dependence of Josephson coupling, then measuring supercurrent nonreciprocity under varying magnetic fields and angles, and finally contrasting these results with junctions deliberately degraded to isolate the source of any observed diode effect.
why_interesting: This work provides a crucial experimental benchmark for understanding superconducting transport in engineered heterostructures, directly addressing how structural control (twist angle) relates to macroscopic quantum phenomena like non-reciprocity, which is relevant for Josephson circuits and quantum devices.
